crossRefs.note: The centurion answered, “Lord, I’m not worthy for you to come under my roof. Just say the word, and my servant will be…
I am not worthy of the least of all the loving kindnesses, and of all the truth, which you have shown to your servant…
“Behold, I am of small account. What will I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth.
I have spoken once, and I will not answer; Yes, twice, but I will proceed no further.”
“I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be restrained.
Against you, and you only, I have sinned, and done that which is evil in your sight, so you may be proved right when…

parallels.note: But she answered him, “Yes, Lord. Yet even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”

translations.web: But she said, “Yes, Lord, but even the dogs eat the crumbs which fall from their masters’ table.”
translations.bsb: “Yes, Lord,” she said, “even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their master’s table.”
translations.kjv: And she said, Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters' table.
translations.asv: But she said, Yea, Lord: for even the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters' table.
